findings.evidence:
Do NOT use when: committing in any other repository, or writing a tag
  annotation or a pull request body, none of which carry this trailer.
findings.note: Scope (this repo, commit messages only) is stated; the procedure otherwise assumes only ordinary git-commit context, which is reasonable to leave implicit.

The command is unquoted so the shell treats ':' -delimited words as extra grep file arguments and parses '<...>' as stdin/stdout redirection, meaning it will error out and can even truncate .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG via the '>' redirect instead of verifying the trailer.

findings.evidence: Run on the same repository before step 1 it exits 1, because the previous message has no such line; run after step 2 it exits 0.
findings.note: The skill's own provenance says it was distilled from this same repo's commit history (repo: dmbritton1/skill-forge, commit 99b0023) where this trailer convention is already in use, so .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG from the prior commit likely already contains 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5' before step 1 ever runs, making grep exit 0 regardless of whether the procedure is followed this time — the check reads stale state, not 'your own commit' as claimed.
